what_it_does: When designing a microchip, engineers must arrange millions of wires and components on a tiny surface in ways that satisfy strict physical rules (called design rules) about minimum spacing, width, and so on. Machine-learning tools that help generate or check these layout patterns need large libraries of labeled examples — but when a new manufacturing process (technology node) is introduced, almost no compliant examples exist yet. PatternPaint tackles this data-scarcity problem by borrowing a diffusion model (the same class of AI that generates photorealistic images from text prompts) and repurposing it for chip layout. Instead of generating a full layout from scratch, it frames the job as inpainting — filling in a missing region of an image given its surroundings — which is an easier task for the model. Fine-tuning requires as few as 20 design-rule-correct example patterns, making it practical to bootstrap a new technology node quickly.
